title: Restic can fail with `Fatal: failed to refresh lock in time` on slow connections
body:
Output of `restic version`
--------------------------
0.15.1

Expected behavior
-----------------
Backups should also be possible over a slow network connection.

Actual behavior
---------------
When uploading over a slow network connection, it is possible that a backup or similar operation fails to refresh lock files within 22.5 minutes and fails with `Fatal: failed to refresh lock in time`. This has been reported on IRC and at least at https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/4157#issuecomment-1408669114 .

<!--
In this section, please try to concentrate on observations, so only describe
what you observed directly.
-->

Steps to reproduce the behavior
-------------------------------
Use a very slow network, then wait for half an hour...
<!--
The more time you spend describing an easy way to reproduce the behavior (if
this is possible), the easier it is for the project developers to fix it!
-->

Do you have any idea what may have caused this?
-----------------------------------------------
restic only allows a limited number of concurrent backend connections. Once all are used for uploading pack files, then a lock file refresh is queued behind them. For a slow connection, it is quite possible that a 16MB pack file (with 5 parallel connections) takes longer than half an hour to upload.

Further fallout from #3569.


Do you have an idea how to solve the issue?
-------------------------------------------
Lock file refreshes should be able to bypass the connections limit.

Hello,

A workaround is to limit concurrent uploads, or what I did and it works (but increase number of files I suppose) is to reduce pack size : RESTIC_PACK_SIZE=4

comments.author: participant3
comments.body: Instead of simulating a slow network, you can also just send a `STOP` signal to restic (`killall -STOP restic`). This pretty much suspends the entire process without killing it, so it can be resumed right where it left off (`killall -CONT restic`). I usually do this when I need to pause the backup to do some other disk intensive stuff, which worked fine until the PR you mentioned was merged. ;_;

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
I have a similar problem using `0.15.1`.I use Wasabi cloud storage using the s3 protocol

 I (foolishly) added two settings I thought would make things go faster, but I guess it only made things worse from what I've read in this thread.
`-o rest.connections=7`
`RESTIC_PACK_SIZE=32`

What's interesting to me, and what may be a different issue from what others have said above is something I saw in my cloud storage logs:
```
"DELETE /bucket123/locks/25e6c40b52ea3bd9d712d10724421b209c6ecaefe7c797b2786706ceedb0eb08" 200 - - 158 905203 0 "" "MinIO (windows; amd64) minio-go/v7.0.47" -
"PUT /bucket123/index/be331dfdcffec1689cd68c747bde8d94b81aba863875198edf0036a2b94cab25" 403 RequestTimeTooSkewed - 0 1313819 0 "" "MinIO (windows; amd64) minio-go/v7.0.47" -
"PUT /bucket123/data/61/6151220fcb80bb0992a3be235d3509cf5bf5cd549ff26ce734de60dd77f612ef" 403 RequestTimeTooSkewed - 0 932476 0 "" "MinIO (windows; amd64) minio-go/v7.0.47" -
```

Notice the `RequestTimeTooSkewed` indications. Does this mean the request was queued and had to wait to long or rather that the whole upload just took too long? I guess there's some kind of request time header in the HTTP request?

For context, I have a 45Mbit connection which was split between 7 separate HTTP PUT requests which comes out to about 800KiB/s. This would take approx 40 minutes to upload the 7x 32MiB packs.

For others experiencing this issue, I recommend leaving the pack size at 16MiB (since you also don't want to quadruple the number of files server-side) and reduce the backend connections to 2 `-o rest.connections=2`

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Notice the `RequestTimeTooSkewed` indications. Does this mean the request was queued and had to wait to long or rather that the whole upload just took too long? I guess there's some kind of request time header in the HTTP request?

That depends on which timestamp Wasabi uses to check the upload against. I'm somewhat sure that it's the moment at which the first part of the request arrives at Wasabi. On the restic side, the connection limit applies before creating the request, so restic would use the timestamp right from the moment when it starts to send the request. So a time skew would have to be introduced somewhere during the upload. However, the most frequent cause of skewed timestamps are not synchronized clocks. Have you check that the hosts clock is correct? Although I have to admit that your workaround suggests that it has something to do with how long the upload takes to complete...

comments.author: participant10
comments.body: It sounds like there are a variety of conditions that could trigger this error message.  I had been pondering the problem descriptions and solutions that have been discussed here, only to discover that my problem more closely matched #4274 (I was running an initial restic backup in a powershell script on a windows 11 laptop that was suspending itself before the backup could complete).  I didn't realize that the laptop suspending itself would triggering that error message, so I thought it was hitting some other problem.  In my case the solution was to change the power management settings so the laptop would not suspend while on AC power.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/4304 should fix most of the issues reported here. If the host suspends while a backup is running, this will still cause the operation to fail, please refer to issue #4262 for that case.


> Addendum 2: No, the restore command has definitely stopped working. Task manager confirms this. restic fails to exit, though. I needed to kill the process by pressing CTRL-C.

@participant8 If you're running an non-Windows OS, then please send a SIGQUIT signal to restic or press Ctrl+/ to send the signal. This causes the go runtime to print a stacktrace and crash restic afterwards.

> We are also observing this same error. Restic v 0.15.1 fails on a slow connection with a rather small backup of about 600MB after about 22 minutes... I would also request you to treat this as a bug please.

How slow is the network connection?

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Just wanted to add that the error "Fatal: failed to refresh lock in time" just occured with 0.15.1 when pausing via "CTRL + Z" and then resuming almost 2 hours later via `fg 1`.

That behavior is currently by design, see https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/4262 .

> I am now doing an index-rebuild

There is no need to rebuild the index.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> Because the added blobs are then in the index and then reused and so a lot of time is saved in the compression step. Or am I wrong and this was really unnecessary and didn't save time for the `backup` command?

`backup` uploads intermediate indexes at least every 10 minutes.
